subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: The Inspired Word of God
overview: The Holy Bible is God's inspired word. In this sub-strand you will learn to handle it with respect, name books in the Old Testament and the New Testament, and recite Isaiah 49:16. You will see why Christians want to read the Bible always.

lessons.title: Handling the Holy Bible with respect
objectives: Explain that the Holy Bible is the inspired word of God.
Show ways of handling the Holy Bible with respect.
lessons.intro: At home you treat a gift from someone you love with care. The Holy Bible is a greater gift. It is God's word, so Christians handle it with respect.
lessons.notes:
The Holy Bible is the book of God's word. Inspired means that God guided the people who wrote it, so what it teaches is His message and not only human ideas. Because it is inspired, we do not treat it like a rough exercise book that we can tear or sit on.

### Why respect it
- It tells us who God is and what He has done.
- It shows us how to live.
- It contains the story of Jesus Christ and His teaching.
- It is the word Christians read in church, at home and at school.

Respecting the Bible is part of respecting God, who gave it.

### Ways to handle it
- Wash your hands before you read, so the pages stay clean.
- Carry it carefully. Do not throw it or swing it.
- Do not place it on the floor or sit on it.
- Turn the pages gently. Do not fold or tear them.
- Do not draw jokes in it or use it to hit someone.
- Keep it in a clean, dry place when you finish.
- Mark a verse with a ribbon or a clean paper, not with food or a dirty stick.
- When it is being read, listen. Do not talk over the reader.

Role-play these actions: one learner pretends to drop the Bible, and another shows the right way to pick it up and dust it with care. Sing a song about respecting the Holy Bible. Responsibility grows when you care for it every day, not only when the teacher is watching.

Reading it is the best respect. A Bible that is never opened is not being honoured. Open it, read a verse, and obey it.

keyWords.meaning: the inspired written word of God
guided by God so that the writing is His word
to treat someone or something as valuable and worthy of care

activity.title: Role-play respectful handling
materials: A ribbon or clean paper for a bookmark
steps: Sing a song related to respecting the Holy Bible.
In groups, role-play ways of handling the Bible with respect and ways that show disrespect.
The class says which actions are right.
Each learner shows how to open the Bible, find a page, and close it gently.

practice.question: What does it mean that the Bible is inspired?
practice.answer: God guided the writers so that the Bible is His word.

practice.question: Give three ways to handle the Holy Bible with respect.
practice.answer: Any three: clean hands, carry it carefully, do not put it on the floor, turn pages gently, do not tear it, store it safely, listen when it is read.

practice.question: Why should Christians respect the Holy Bible?
practice.answer: Because it is the inspired word of God.

summary: The Holy Bible is the inspired word of God.
Handle it gently, keep it clean, and do not throw or tear it.
The greatest respect is to read it and obey it.

lessons.title: Books of the Old and New Testament
objectives: Identify books in the Old Testament and the New Testament.
Role-play and play games that name some Bible books.
lessons.intro: The Bible is one book made of many smaller books. They are grouped into two main parts: the Old Testament and the New Testament. Knowing the names helps you find a verse when the teacher says "Luke" or "Genesis."
lessons.notes:
A testament here is a covenant, a binding agreement between God and His people. The Old Testament tells of God's work before the birth of Jesus Christ. The New Testament tells of Jesus Christ and the first Christians.

The Old Testament has 39 books. The New Testament has 27 books. Together the Bible has 66 books.

### Some Old Testament books
The first five are Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy. Other books you will meet in Grade 4 are Judges, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, Psalms, Proverbs and Isaiah. The Old Testament also has books such as Joshua, Ruth, Job, Jeremiah and Malachi. Malachi is the last book of the Old Testament.

### Some New Testament books
The first four are the Gospels: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. They tell the life of Jesus. Acts comes next. Then there are letters, such as Romans, 1 Corinthians, Ephesians and Philippians. The last book is Revelation.

### How to tell them apart
If the story is about Abraham, Joseph, Samson, Balaam or the creation of the world, you are in the Old Testament. If the story is about the birth of Jesus, His miracles or His teaching in parables, you are in the New Testament.

### Naming games
In pairs, read a chart of the books. One learner calls "Old" or "New," and the partner names a book from that part. You can also role-play: hold a card that says "Exodus" or "John" and stand in the correct group. Counting the books uses the same careful counting you use in Mathematics. Knowing the names helps you respect the Bible by finding your place quickly.

keyWords.meaning: the first part of the Bible, with 39 books, written before the birth of Jesus
the second part of the Bible, with 27 books, about Jesus and the first Christians
one of the four books that tell the life and teaching of Jesus: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John

examples.problem: The teacher says, "Open Luke 19." Is Luke in the Old Testament or the New Testament?
steps: Luke is one of the four Gospels.
The Gospels tell the life of Jesus.
They are in the New Testament.
examples.answer: Luke is in the New Testament.

activity.title: Chart reading and a naming game
steps: In pairs, observe and read a chart of books in the Old and New Testament.
Count the Old Testament books and the New Testament books.
Play a game: a leader calls Old or New, and a learner names a book from that part.
Role-play naming books by holding a card and standing in the Old or New group.
Sing a song about the books in the Holy Bible.

practice.question: How many books are in the Old Testament, the New Testament, and the whole Bible?
practice.answer: 39 in the Old Testament, 27 in the New Testament, and 66 altogether.

practice.question: Is Genesis in the Old Testament or the New Testament?
Name two Old Testament books and two New Testament books.
practice.answer: Any correct pair, for example Genesis and Psalms; Luke and Acts.

summary: The Old Testament has 39 books and the New Testament has 27 books.
The Gospels are Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.
Games and charts help you name the books and find them quickly.

lessons.title: Isaiah 49:16 and the desire to read
objectives: Give reasons for reading the Holy Bible always.
lessons.intro: People write a name on a hand so they will not forget. God uses a picture like that in Isaiah 49:16. He does not forget His people. The Bible is where we keep meeting the God who remembers us.
lessons.notes:
Isaiah 49:16 says that God has engraved His people on the palms of His hands. Their walls are always before Him. Engraved means cut or written so that it stays. God is telling His people that He cannot forget them. He keeps them in view, as if their name were written on His hand.

### Meditating on the verse
Read the verse slowly. Sit quietly. Think: God does not forget His people. I am one of the people He calls. He wants me to know Him. Recite the verse until you can say it without the book. This practice builds spiritual awareness, a heart that notices God.

### Why read the Bible always
- It is God's inspired word, so it tells the truth about Him.
- It reminds you that God does not forget you, as Isaiah 49:16 says.
- It shows the right way when you must make a choice.
- It introduces Jesus Christ, the Saviour.
- It gives verses to recite when you are afraid, angry or thankful.
- Reading every day keeps the habit alive. A verse a day is a good beginning.

Choose a regular time: after waking, or before you sleep. Keep the Bible where you can reach it. Ask a parent to listen while you read one short passage. When you desire to read always, you are treating the Bible as a friend you return to, not as a book you open only in an examination week.

Sing a song about the books of the Bible, then close by reciting Isaiah 49:16 together.

keyWords.meaning: written or cut in a lasting way
to think quietly and carefully about a verse

activity.title: Recite and meditate on Isaiah 49:16
steps: Write it on a flash card.
Recite it in pairs, then sit quietly and meditate on the promise that God does not forget His people.
Each learner says one reason for reading the Bible always.
Sing a song about the books in the Holy Bible.

practice.question: What picture does Isaiah 49:16 use?
practice.answer: God has engraved His people on the palms of His hands, so He does not forget them.

practice.question: What does engraved mean?
practice.answer: Written or cut in a lasting way.

practice.question: Give two reasons to read the Holy Bible always.
practice.answer: Any two: it is God's word; it reminds us God does not forget His people; it guides choices; it tells us about Jesus; it helps us when we are afraid or thankful.

summary: Isaiah 49:16 says God has engraved His people on the palms of His hands.
God does not forget His people.
Christians desire to read the Bible always because it is His word.

quiz.question: The Holy Bible is called inspired because...
options: God guided the writers so that it is His word
quiz.explanation: Inspiration means God guided the writing of Scripture.

quiz.question: Which action shows respect for the Bible?
quiz.explanation: Gentle handling keeps the Bible clean and honours God's word.

quiz.question: Why should you respect the Holy Bible?
quiz.answer: Because it is the inspired word of God.
quiz.explanation: Respect follows from knowing whose word it is.

quiz.question: How many books are in the New Testament?
quiz.explanation: The New Testament has 27 books. The Old Testament has 39. Together they make 66.

quiz.question: Which book is in the Old Testament?
quiz.explanation: Genesis is the first book of the Old Testament.

quiz.question: The four Gospels are...
quiz.explanation: These four New Testament books tell the life and teaching of Jesus.

quiz.question: A naming game in class helps learners to...
options: name books in the Old and New Testament
quiz.explanation: The learning experience includes games on naming Bible books.

quiz.question: Isaiah 49:16 teaches that God...
options: has engraved His people on the palms of His hands
quiz.explanation: The verse uses the picture of engraving so that God's people are not forgotten.

quiz.question: Why should you desire to read the Bible always?
quiz.answer: Because it is God's word and it helps me know Him, including His promise not to forget His people.
quiz.explanation: Isaiah 49:16 and the inspiration of Scripture give reasons to keep reading.

quiz.question: The Old Testament has how many books?
quiz.explanation: There are 39 books in the Old Testament.
